name: Riyadh Air
desc: New Saudi full-service airline that began commercial flights in October 2025 from its Riyadh hub.
capacity_detail: Front-of-shirt sponsor of Atlético Madrid since 2023 and naming rights to the Metropolitano stadium since 2024
sponsorships: Atlético Madrid shirt (2023); CONCACAF official airline (2024); Metropolitano naming rights (2024); WTA Finals co-sponsor (2024)
markets: Riyadh hub with routes to Europe, South and South-East Asia, the Middle East and North Africa, including the UK, Spain, India, Malaysia

signals.regions: Added Mumbai, Jakarta and Milan routes during 2026 (Aug-Dec 2026; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riyadh_Air)

rationale: Newly launched flag carrier needs global brand awareness fast; Gulf rivals Emirates, Etihad and Qatar Airways have all used F1.

name: Emirates
desc: Dubai-based international airline flying to more than 150 cities in 80 countries across six continents.
ownership: state fund: Investment Corporation of Dubai
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 34.83bn in fiscal 2024-25
sponsorships: Arsenal, Real Madrid, AC Milan, Benfica, Olympique Lyonnais shirts; NBA official airline (2024); tennis majors; Rugby World Cup; LA Dodgers; F1 official airline 2013-2022 (ended)
markets: Six continents: Europe, the Americas, Africa, Middle East, South Asia, East Asia and Australia
rationale: Former F1 official airline (2013-2022) lost the slot to Qatar Airways; a team deal would restore its motorsport presence.

name: flydubai
desc: Dubai government-owned low-cost airline operating more than 130 destinations from Dubai International Airport.
ownership: state fund: Investment Corporation of Dubai
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 3.6bn in 2024
markets: Middle East, Central Asia, South Asia, Africa, Eastern Europe and the Caucasus from its Dubai hub
rationale: Growing low-cost carrier with a 150-aircraft Airbus order could use F1 to lift brand recognition beyond its regional base.

name: Jumeirah Group
desc: Dubai luxury hotel company managing beach resorts, city hotels and serviced residences in twelve countries.
capacity_detail: Owned by Dubai Holding, the Dubai ruler's state-owned global investment holding company, and expanding abroad
markets: Hotels in the UAE, Gulf states, China, Indonesia, the Maldives, Spain, Italy, the UK and Switzerland
rationale: Luxury hotel brand expanding in Europe and Asia; F1 hospitality audiences match its high-spending guest profile, as Hilton and Hyatt show.

name: Red Sea Global
desc: Saudi developer and operator of luxury tourism destinations The Red Sea and AMAALA on the Red Sea coast.
capacity_detail: Owned by the Public Investment Fund; marketing its resorts to international travellers
sponsorships: Al-Ahli Saudi FC platinum sponsor (2023, moved to AMAALA in Aug 2026); T1 esports three-year deal (2025); The Ocean Race grand finale host (2027)
markets: Resorts in Saudi Arabia marketed to international luxury travellers from Europe, Asia and the Gulf
rationale: Needs affluent international visitors for its Red Sea resorts; F1's premium global audience and Saudi Grand Prix link fit well.

name: NEOM
desc: Saudi company developing the NEOM economic zone in Tabuk Province, including Oxagon, Trojena and Sindalah.
capacity_detail: Wholly owned by the Public Investment Fund, with brand offices opened in London and New York
sponsorships: Title sponsor of NEOM McLaren Electric Racing in Formula E and Extreme E (from 2022); McLaren F1 Academy entries (2026); Asian Football Confederation (2021); Mercedes-EQ Formula E (2020)
markets: Saudi Arabia, marketing internationally through offices in London and New York
rationale: Already backs McLaren's F1 Academy entries; an F1 team deal would extend existing motorsport marketing, though the project is being scaled back.

name: Qiddiya Investment Company
desc: Saudi developer of Qiddiya City, an entertainment, sport and culture destination with Six Flags and Aquarabia.
capacity_detail: FIFA World Cup 2026 official tournament supporter through PIF's partnership (May 2026)
sponsorships: FIFA World Cup 2026 tournament supporter via PIF (2026)
markets: Riyadh destination marketed to Saudi, Gulf and international visitors
rationale: Building an FIA Grade 1 circuit planned for Formula One; partnering with F1 now would build awareness before the track opens.

name: Savvy Games Group
desc: Saudi games and esports group that owns ESL, FACEIT, Scopely and Niantic's former games business.
capacity_detail: FIFA World Cup 2026 official tournament supporter through PIF's partnership (May 2026)
sponsorships: FIFA World Cup 2026 tournament supporter via PIF (2026); Al Hilal main shirt sponsor (2023-2026)
markets: Games and esports businesses in Germany, the UK, the United States and Saudi Arabia, with players worldwide

signals.raise: Announced USD 6bn purchase of Moonton from ByteDance (Mar 2026; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savvy_Games_Group)

rationale: Gaming and esports audiences overlap with F1's young fan base; games brands such as PUBG Mobile already sponsor F1 teams.

name: Scopely
desc: Mobile games publisher in Culver City, California, owned by Saudi Arabia's Savvy Games Group.
capacity_detail: Owned by PIF's Savvy Games Group, which bought it for USD 4.9bn in 2023
markets: Mobile games played worldwide, with studios in the United States and abroad
rationale: Mobile game publishers use F1 for mass reach; PUBG Mobile's team deals show the model works for player acquisition.

name: Electronic Arts
desc: Video game publisher of EA Sports FC, Madden NFL, NHL and other titles, taken private in 2026.
capacity_detail: Bought for about USD 55bn by PIF, Silver Lake and Affinity Partners; delisted on completion 4 Aug 2026
sponsorships: Licensed games for NFL, NHL, NBA, UFC, PGA Tour, NASCAR and WRC
markets: Players and studios across North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific
rationale: Major sports-game publisher with motor-racing titles; F1 partnership would support its racing franchises among motorsport fans.

name: Newcastle United
desc: English Premier League football club based at St James' Park, majority owned by Saudi Arabia's PIF.
capacity_detail: Public Investment Fund holds 85% (RB Sports & Media 15%) since the October 2021 takeover
sponsorships: Club itself; front-of-shirt sponsors Sela (2023-2026) and Knox Hydrate (2026-)
markets: Premier League club with fans across the UK, Europe, the Middle East, Asia and North America
rationale: PIF is building the club into a global brand; F1 cross-promotion suits its partner Saudi brands and Premier League audience.

name: Al Nassr
desc: Saudi Pro League football club in Riyadh, 2025-26 league champions, majority owned by the Public Investment Fund.
capacity_detail: Public Investment Fund holds 75%, Al-Nassr Non-Profit Foundation 25%
sponsorships: Club itself; kit supplier adidas (2024-2027); shirt sponsor Humain (2026-)
markets: Saudi Arabia, with an international fan base built through signings such as Cristiano Ronaldo
rationale: A globally followed club since Ronaldo's arrival; joint content with an F1 team could widen its fan base beyond football.

name: Sela
desc: Saudi events, entertainment and hospitality company running venues such as Boulevard City and Jeddah Superdome.
capacity_detail: Owned by the Public Investment Fund; opened its first international office, in London, in March 2025
sponsorships: Newcastle United front-of-shirt sponsor (2023-2026); promoter of major boxing events
markets: Saudi Arabia, with an office in London and international sports and entertainment events
rationale: Events company that already sponsors Premier League football; F1 race-weekend hospitality and events fit its business.

name: Ceer Motors
desc: Saudi electric car brand developing sedans and SUVs for the Gulf region, with seven models planned by 2030.
capacity_detail: Owned by the Public Investment Fund; launching EVs for the GCC region
markets: Saudi Arabia and the wider GCC region

signals.raise: Signed 16 agreements worth SAR 3.7bn to localise EV manufacturing (Feb 2026; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ceer_Motors)

rationale: New car brand needs fast credibility and awareness; motorsport association is a classic route for launching an EV marque.

name: Dubai Duty Free
desc: Airport duty-free retailer operating shops at Dubai International and Al Maktoum International airports.
ownership: state fund: Investment Corporation of Dubai
capacity_detail: Sales about USD 2.16bn in 2023
markets: Dubai airports, selling to travellers from around the world
rationale: Sells luxury, spirits and fragrance to global travellers; F1 hospitality and premium brand partners mirror its retail mix.

name: EDGE Group
desc: Abu Dhabi government-owned defence and technology group making weapons, drones and military systems for export.
ownership: state fund: Government of Abu Dhabi
capacity_detail: Owned by the Government of Abu Dhabi and expanding exports and joint ventures abroad
markets: UAE plus export customers and partners in Angola, Brazil, Kenya, Indonesia, Turkey, India, Italy and Estonia

signals.regions: Formed Edge-Anduril Production Alliance with US firm Anduril (Nov 2025; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EDGE_Group)

rationale: Engineering brand courting international partners; F1 technical partnerships suit recruitment, though defence branding limits fit.

name: Harrods
desc: Luxury department store in Knightsbridge, London, owned by the Qatar Investment Authority since 2010.
capacity_detail: Owned by the Qatar Investment Authority since May 2010
markets: London flagship serving shoppers from the UK, Europe, the Middle East and Asia
rationale: Global luxury retail brand; F1's wealthy international audience and luxury partner roster suit its customer base.

name: Qatari Diar
desc: Qatari real estate developer headquartered in Lusail, wholly controlled by the Qatar Investment Authority.
capacity_detail: Wholly controlled by the Qatar Investment Authority
markets: Qatar and international property projects
rationale: Developer promoting Qatari projects to international investors; F1 Qatar Grand Prix gives a home platform for buyer events.

name: Katara Hospitality
desc: Qatari government-owned hotel owner, developer and operator with properties in Qatar, Europe, Africa and Asia.
capacity_detail: Owned by the Qatar Investment Authority; hotels in 12 countries
sponsorships: La Liga partnership for a La Liga Lounge in Doha (2017)
markets: Hotels in Qatar, Egypt, Morocco, the UK, France, Italy, Switzerland, Spain, the Netherlands, the US, Singapore and Thailand
rationale: Owner of landmark European luxury hotels; F1 hospitality suits its high-end guests, as Hilton and Hyatt deals show.

name: Paris Saint-Germain
desc: French football club, back-to-back UEFA Champions League winners, owned mainly by Qatar Sports Investments.
capacity_detail: Qatar Sports Investments, linked to the State of Qatar, holds 85.9%
sponsorships: Club itself; UEFA Champions League winners 2025 and 2026
markets: Ligue 1 club with a global fan base across Europe, the Americas, Asia and the Middle East
rationale: A lifestyle sports brand building global reach; F1's fashion-and-celebrity audience overlaps closely with PSG's brand strategy.

name: Mapletree Investments
desc: Singapore real estate developer and investment manager owning and managing properties in 13 markets worldwide.
capacity_detail: Revenue SGD 2.86bn in 2023 (about USD 2.1bn)
markets: Properties in Singapore, Australia, Canada, China, Europe, Hong Kong, India, Japan, Malaysia, South Korea, the UK, the US and Vietnam
rationale: Global property manager seeking institutional investors; F1 Singapore hospitality offers a business-entertainment platform.

name: PSA International
desc: Singapore port group operating container terminals across a network spanning 45 countries.
capacity_detail: Revenue SGD 8.264bn in 2025 (about USD 6.2bn)
markets: Terminals in 45 countries across Asia, Europe, the Americas and the Middle East
rationale: Global logistics rivals DP World and DHL already use F1; PSA could match them for B2B brand visibility.

name: Surbana Jurong
desc: Singapore urban, infrastructure and engineering consultancy with about 15,000 employees and global acquisitions.
capacity_detail: Wholly owned by Temasek; expanded internationally through acquisitions such as SMEC and Robert Bird Group
markets: Asia, Australia, Africa, the Middle East, Europe and the Americas through acquired firms
rationale: Engineering consultancy competing for global talent and contracts; rivals like AtkinsRéalis already sponsor F1 teams.

name: Malaysia Airlines
desc: Malaysian national airline flying from Kuala Lumpur International Airport to 69 destinations.
capacity_detail: Associate sponsor and official global airline partner of IPL franchise Mumbai Indians (announced Jan 2026)
sponsorships: Mumbai Indians IPL partnership (Jan 2026); Manchester United Asian Tour official airline
markets: Kuala Lumpur hub serving South-East Asia, East Asia, South Asia, Australia, the Middle East and Europe

signals.marketing: New group CEO Nasaruddin Bakar replaced Izham Ismail (Feb 2026; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaysia_Airlines)

rationale: Rebuilding its brand under a new plan; rivals Singapore Airlines and Qatar Airways use F1 for premium travel marketing.

name: Oman Air
desc: Omani flag carrier flying from Muscat to 43 destinations in 25 countries.
capacity_detail: Parent company is the Oman Investment Authority
sponsorships: Chelsea FC global airline partner (2023, reported possibly ended 2024); NBO Golf Classic presenting sponsor (2015)
markets: Muscat hub serving the Gulf, South Asia, South-East Asia, Africa and Europe

signals.regions: Resumed Singapore service after nine years (Jul 2026; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oman_Air)

rationale: Small flag carrier promoting Oman tourism; Gulf Air's F1 deal shows how regional airlines use F1 for awareness.

name: Royal Air Maroc
desc: Moroccan state-owned flag carrier flying from Casablanca to more than 100 destinations.
ownership: state fund: Government of Morocco and Hassan II Fund
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 1.7bn in fiscal 2017
sponsorships: 2025 Africa Cup of Nations aircraft livery
markets: Africa, Europe, the Middle East and the Americas from Casablanca

signals.regions: Opened a Tetouan base and six European routes (Jan 2026; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Air_Maroc)

rationale: Growing as Morocco prepares to co-host the 2030 World Cup; F1 would raise its premium profile in Europe.

name: EgyptAir
desc: Egyptian state-owned flag carrier flying from Cairo to 84 international destinations in 56 countries.
capacity_detail: Exclusive official airline partner of FC Barcelona football, basketball and handball teams through 2028/29 (Aug 2026)
sponsorships: FC Barcelona global airline partner through 2028/29 (2026)
markets: Africa, the Middle East, Europe, Asia and North America from Cairo

signals.regions: Launched Cairo-Los Angeles (May 2026) and Cairo-Chicago (Jun 2026) services (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EgyptAir)

rationale: Expanding into US markets with new long-haul routes; F1's American and European audiences support Egypt tourism marketing.

name: Ethiopian Airlines
desc: Ethiopian state-owned airline flying to 145 international passenger destinations from Addis Ababa.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 7.0bn in fiscal 2024
markets: Africa, Europe, the Middle East, Asia and the Americas from its Addis Ababa hub
rationale: Africa's largest airline expanding long-haul; F1 would lift its brand among European and Asian premium travellers.

name: Pertamina
desc: Indonesian state energy company producing oil and gas and selling fuels and lubricants under its own brands.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 84.89bn in 2023
sponsorships: Indonesian MotoGP and Mandalika circuit main sponsor (2022); VR46 Racing Team; Moto2 Mandalika Racing Team (2021); Lamborghini Super Trofeo title sponsor (2015); Manor F1 driver backing (2016)
markets: Indonesia plus overseas operations in Iraq, Vietnam, Malaysia, Algeria, Libya, Qatar and Australia
rationale: Long-time motorsport sponsor with a lubricants brand to export; F1 would match rival Petronas's global exposure.

name: Viettel
desc: Vietnamese state-owned telecom and technology group operating mobile networks in Vietnam and ten other countries.
ownership: state fund: Government of Vietnam (Ministry of National Defence)
capacity_detail: Revenue about USD 7.25bn in 2023
sponsorships: Peru national team telecom provider at the 2018 FIFA World Cup; owns Thể Công-Viettel FC
markets: Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia, Myanmar, Timor-Leste, Haiti, Peru, Mozambique, Tanzania, Cameroon and Burundi
rationale: Telecom group building an international brand; rivals such as STC and Tata Communications use F1 for B2B reach.

name: FAW Group
desc: Chinese state-owned carmaker producing Hongqi and Bestune cars and Jiefang trucks, exporting to over 80 countries.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 89.5bn in 2023
markets: China plus exports to more than 80 countries and plants in Pakistan, South Africa, Tanzania, Vietnam and Russia

signals.raise: Agreed to buy 5% of Leapmotor for about CNY 3.74bn (Dec 2025; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FAW_Group)

rationale: Pushing Hongqi as a luxury export brand; F1 is the established route for carmakers to gain premium credibility abroad.

name: Azerbaijan Airlines
desc: Azerbaijani state-owned flag carrier flying to 57 destinations from Heydar Aliyev International Airport.
ownership: state fund: Government of Azerbaijan (AZCON Holding)
capacity_detail: Revenue AZN 1.149bn in 2022 (about USD 676m)
markets: Caucasus, Central Asia, Russia, Europe, the Middle East and Asia from Baku
rationale: Home carrier of the Baku Grand Prix city; F1 sponsorship would promote Baku as a transit hub to European travellers.

name: Uzbekistan Airways
desc: Uzbek state-owned flag carrier flying to 58 destinations from Tashkent and expanding its wide-body fleet.
capacity_detail: Owned by the Government of Uzbekistan; doubling its fleet by 2030 and adding international routes
markets: Central Asia, Russia, Turkey, the Middle East, China, South Asia and Europe from Tashkent

signals.regions: Added Andijan-Istanbul, Tashkent-Atyrau and new China routes (early 2026; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uzbekistan_Airways)

rationale: Expanding fast with 22 Boeing 787s on order; F1 would build awareness for Uzbekistan tourism and transit.

name: Kuwait Airways
desc: Kuwaiti government-owned flag carrier flying from Kuwait International Airport to about 50 destinations.
capacity_detail: Wholly owned by the Government of Kuwait
markets: Middle East, South Asia, Europe, North Africa and North America from Kuwait
rationale: Competing with larger Gulf carriers that use F1 heavily; a deal would raise visibility, but budget appetite is uncertain.

name: TAP Air Portugal
desc: Portuguese flag carrier flying from Lisbon to 87 destinations, strong in Brazil, Africa and North America.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 4,242m in 2024 (about USD 4.7bn)
markets: Europe, Brazil, Africa and North America from Lisbon and Porto

signals.ipo: Government selected Lufthansa's bid for up to 49.9% (Oct 2026; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TAP_Air_Portugal)

rationale: Being part-privatised to Lufthansa; a new owner may refresh marketing, and F1's growing US audience suits its transatlantic network.

name: SNCF
desc: French state-owned railway group running TGV, Ouigo, Eurostar and Keolis passenger services in France and abroad.
ownership: state fund: Agence des participations de l'État
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 41.4bn in 2022 (about USD 45.5bn)
markets: France plus Ouigo España in Spain, Eurostar to the UK, Belgium and the Netherlands, Lyria to Switzerland and Keolis worldwide
rationale: Competing for travellers in Spain and on cross-border routes; rail-versus-air messaging could use F1's European audience, though fit is weak.

name: Ferrovie dello Stato Italiane
desc: Italian state-owned railway group running Trenitalia and rail operations in Germany, Greece, the UK, France and Spain.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 14.8bn in 2023 (about USD 16.3bn)
markets: Italy plus Germany (Netinera), Greece (Hellenic Train), UK (Avanti stake), France, Spain (Iryo) and the Netherlands
rationale: Expanding Frecciarossa high-speed services across Europe; Italian Grand Prix audiences in Monza and Imola are natural customers.

name: LOT Polish Airlines
desc: Polish state-owned flag carrier flying from Warsaw to about 100 destinations in Europe, Asia and North America.
ownership: state fund: Polish Aviation Group (State Treasury)
capacity_detail: Revenue PLN 10.22bn in 2025 (about USD 2.7bn)
markets: Central and Eastern Europe, Western Europe, Asia and North America from Warsaw
rationale: Building Warsaw as a regional hub against Gulf and Turkish carriers; F1 offers premium brand reach at moderate scale.

name: Aerolíneas Argentinas
desc: Argentine state-owned flag carrier operating domestic and international flights from Buenos Aires hubs.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 1.33bn in fiscal 2019
markets: Argentina, South America, plus routes to North America and Europe
rationale: State flag carrier awaiting privatisation; F1 would raise its profile on routes to North America and Europe, but budget is tight.

name: Kazakhstan Temir Zholy
desc: Kazakh national railway company running freight and passenger rail and China-Europe transit logistics corridors.
capacity_detail: Revenue KZT 1,173.3bn in 2020 (about USD 2.8bn)
markets: Kazakhstan with rail links to Russia, China, Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan and transit to Europe
rationale: Marketing the trans-Caspian corridor to global shippers; F1 B2B hospitality could help, though consumer fit is weak.

name: SOCAR
industry: state oil company and fuel retailer
desc: Azerbaijani state oil and gas company that also runs SOCAR-branded fuel stations in six European countries.
capacity_detail: Revenue AZN 119.2bn in 2022 (about USD 70bn)
sponsorships: UEFA Euro 2016 official sponsor (2014-2017, ended 2021); Baku 2015 European Games partner; 2019 Azerbaijan Grand Prix title sponsor; Galatasaray chest sponsor (from 2023-24); Neftchi Baku
markets: Azerbaijan plus fuel retail in Georgia, Turkey, Ukraine, Romania, Switzerland and Austria

signals.regions: Completed acquisition of Italy's Gruppo API (Q2 2026; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SOCAR)

rationale: Former title sponsor of the Baku Grand Prix with a European fuel-retail brand; F1 would rebuild that consumer visibility.

name: beIN Media Group
desc: Qatari state-owned sports and entertainment broadcaster operating in 43 countries across five continents in seven languages.
capacity_detail: Owned and funded by the State of Qatar; broadcasting in 43 countries
sponsorships: Broadcaster of FIFA Club World Cup (2019, 2020); LA 2028 Olympic media rights (reported Feb 2026)
markets: Middle East and North Africa, Europe, North America, Asia-Pacific and Australia
rationale: Sports broadcaster whose subscriptions depend on premium rights; an F1 partnership could support motorsport content and subscriber marketing.

name: dnata
desc: Dubai aviation services group providing ground handling, cargo, flight catering and travel services in 84 countries.
ownership: state fund: Investment Corporation of Dubai
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 3.6bn in 2018
markets: 84 countries and 129 airports across the Middle East, Europe, Asia-Pacific, Africa and the Americas

signals.marketing: Sold Travel Republic and Netflights brands to Destinia (Jan 2026; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dnata)

rationale: Global aviation services brand; F1's travelling logistics and hospitality operation suits catering and cargo partnership showcases.

name: Dongfeng Motor Corporation
desc: Chinese state-owned carmaker producing Dongfeng, Voyah and M-Hero vehicles, with joint ventures with Nissan and Stellantis.
capacity_detail: Revenue CNY 601.5bn in 2018 (about USD 91bn)
markets: China plus exports to the Middle East, Africa, South Asia and planned Voyah sales in Europe

signals.regions: Announced Stellantis-led joint venture to sell Voyah vehicles in Europe (May 2026; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dongfeng_Motor_Corporation)

rationale: Launching premium Voyah EVs in Europe with Stellantis; F1 offers fast credibility for a new premium brand.

name: COMAC
desc: Chinese state-owned maker of commercial airliners including the C909 regional jet and C919 narrow-body.
capacity_detail: State-owned, founded by SASAC and state groups; marketing the C919 against Airbus and Boeing
markets: Mainly Chinese airlines, with 1,317 orders, and efforts to win foreign customers
rationale: Seeking international credibility against Airbus and Boeing; F1 engineering prestige could help, though state links limit Western deals.

name: OCP Group
desc: Moroccan state-owned phosphate miner and fertiliser maker selling to more than 160 customers on five continents.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 9.76bn in 2024
markets: Africa (16 countries), North America, Brazil, India and Asia-Pacific
rationale: Mainly B2B fertiliser seller; F1 hospitality could serve agribusiness clients, but consumer brand fit is limited.

name: Air Algérie
desc: Algerian state-owned flag carrier flying domestic routes and to about 44 international destinations.
capacity_detail: Sales turnover DZD 113.6bn in 2018 (about USD 960m)
markets: Algeria, Europe, Africa, the Middle East and North America
rationale: Expanding European routes such as Berlin; F1 is a stretch given its budget, but builds awareness in Europe.

name: ÖBB
desc: Austrian state-owned railway group running domestic trains and Europe's largest Nightjet night-train fleet.
capacity_detail: Wholly owned by the Republic of Austria; operates Nightjet services across Europe
markets: Austria and neighbouring Germany, Switzerland, Italy, Czech Republic, Hungary, Slovakia, Slovenia and Liechtenstein
rationale: Promoting Nightjet as low-carbon travel across Europe; the Austrian Grand Prix gives a home market platform.

name: Eurostar
desc: High-speed rail operator linking London, Paris, Brussels, Amsterdam and Cologne, majority owned by France's SNCF.
capacity_detail: SNCF, wholly owned by the French state, holds 55%; expanding routes
markets: UK, France, Belgium, the Netherlands and Germany, with planned routes to Switzerland and Frankfurt

signals.regions: Agreement with SBB and SNCF paving way for London-Switzerland services (2026; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eurostar)

rationale: Competes with airlines on London-Europe routes; F1 European race weekends could promote rail travel to events.

name: Diriyah Company
desc: Saudi developer of the Diriyah heritage and lifestyle destination near Riyadh, owned by the Public Investment Fund.
capacity_detail: Sponsor and host of the Formula E Diriyah E-Prix (Jan 2024), and sponsor of tennis, equestrian and boxing events
sponsorships: Formula E Diriyah E-Prix sponsor (2024); Diriyah Saudi Super Cup title sponsor (2023, 2024); tennis, equestrian and boxing events
markets: Riyadh destination marketed to Saudi residents and international visitors and investors
rationale: Already uses Formula E to promote the destination; an F1 tie-in around the Saudi Grand Prix would extend that reach.

name: COSCO Shipping
desc: Chinese state-owned shipping group running container lines, terminals and logistics, including Greece's Piraeus port.
capacity_detail: Revenue USD 44.66bn in 2020
markets: Shipping and ports worldwide, including Piraeus in Greece, Khalifa Port in the UAE and Khorgos in Kazakhstan
rationale: Shipping rivals MSC and logistics firms DHL and DP World use F1 for B2B reach; US security disputes limit fit.

name: AROYA Cruises
desc: Saudi cruise line sailing in the Arabian Gulf, Red Sea and Mediterranean, run by PIF-owned Cruise Saudi.
capacity_detail: Flagship cruise line of Cruise Saudi, a Public Investment Fund company, sailing internationally
sponsorships: Al Nassr kit sponsor (since 2023, renewed for 2026-27); Yalla Aroya campaign with Cristiano Ronaldo
markets: Gulf, Red Sea and Mediterranean itineraries visiting Saudi Arabia, Qatar, UAE, Türkiye, Greece, Egypt and Jordan

signals.regions: Summer 2026 Mediterranean season from Istanbul to Türkiye, Greece and Egypt (Jul 2026; https://www.rustourismnews.com/2026/07/30/aroya-cruises-extends-partnership-with-cristiano-ronaldos-al-nassr/)

rationale: Cruise rivals MSC Cruises and Regent Seven Seas sponsor F1; AROYA needs European and Gulf awareness for its new ship.

name: Air Serbia
desc: Serbian government-owned flag carrier flying from Belgrade to 89 destinations in 35 countries.
capacity_detail: Revenue EUR 719.5m in 2025 (about USD 791m)
markets: Balkans, Western and Northern Europe, the Middle East, North America and China from Belgrade, Niš and Morava

signals.marketing: Launched own Elevate frequent-flyer programme replacing Etihad Guest (Jun 2026; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_Serbia)

rationale: Building Belgrade as a Balkan hub with its own loyalty scheme; F1 is ambitious for its size but boosts premium awareness.

name: SriLankan Airlines
desc: Sri Lankan government-owned flag carrier flying from Colombo to 33 destinations in 21 countries.
ownership: state fund: Government of Sri Lanka
capacity_detail: Revenue LKR 365.171bn in 2023 (about USD 1.1bn)
sponsorships: Colombo Marathon
markets: South Asia, South-East Asia, East Asia, the Middle East, Europe and Australia from Colombo
rationale: Promotes Sri Lanka tourism to Europe and Asia; budget pressures after restructuring make F1 a long shot.
